topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-First Way to Trace Contacts

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Centralized vs. Decentralized
lecture_lines: Digital contact tracing helps slow pandemic spread.
Centralized systems track user identities and locations.
This creates a "Big Brother" privacy risk.
DP-3T offers a decentralized, privacy-preserving alternative.
Users control their own data without a central tracker.
animations: Show a central server icon (#FFFFFF) labeled 'Centralized Server' at the top and 4 phone icons (#00FF00) at the bottom. Draw lines connecting each phone to the server.
Change lines to red (#FF0000) and display a large eye icon (#FF0000) over the server to represent surveillance. Text: 'Privacy Risk'.
Remove the server and lines. Each phone icon now displays a small folder icon (#FFFF00) labeled 'Local Log'. Text: 'DP-3T: Decentralized Approach'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: One-Way Hash Functions & PRFs
lecture_lines: Cryptographic hashes create unique, irreversible digital fingerprints.
Pseudo-Random Functions derive secure IDs from secret keys.
These building blocks ensure data remains anonymous.
animations: Display a box labeled 'Hash Function H(x)' (#FF8C00) in the center. An arrow labeled 'Input Data' (#FFFFFF) points into it.
A random hex string 'a8f3...12' (#00BFFF) emerges from the box. Label it 'Unique Hash'.
Display a red 'X' (#FF0000) over a reverse arrow pointing back to the input, indicating the function is one-way.

sections.title: Step 1: Generating Daily Keys and Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
lecture_lines: Each phone generates a unique Secret Day Key.
Multiple Ephemeral IDs derive from this daily key.
These IDs change frequently to prevent tracking.
Ephemeral IDs look random to any outside observer.
This hierarchy keeps the user's identity hidden.
animations: Display 'SK_t (Secret Day Key)' (#00BFFF) at the top center.
Branch out 4 lines to 4 nodes labeled 'EphID_1' to 'EphID_4' (#1E90FF) below the key.
Show a clock icon (#FFFFFF) next to EphID_1 showing '12:00 PM'.
The clock moves to '12:15 PM', and EphID_1 fades while EphID_2 highlights to show rotation.
Add text 'Rotating IDs prevent long-term tracking' (#FFFF00) at the bottom.

sections.title: Step 2: The Bluetooth Handshake (Broadcasting)
lecture_lines: Phones broadcast Ephemeral IDs via Bluetooth Low Energy.
Nearby devices exchange and store IDs locally.
Handshakes happen without identifying the users.
animations: Place Alice's phone (#00FF00) and Bob's phone (#FF00FF) on opposite sides of the screen.
Alice's phone pulses with circles (#FFFFFF), sending 'EphID_A' towards Bob.
Bob's phone receives 'EphID_A' and adds it to a 'Local Log' icon.
Bob's phone pulses with circles, sending 'EphID_B' back to Alice.
Alice's phone adds 'EphID_B' to its own 'Local Log' icon.

sections.title: Step 3: Reporting a Positive Case
lecture_lines: Infected users voluntarily upload their Secret Day Keys.
No personal contact logs are sent to the server.
The server only hosts keys of infected individuals.
animations: Alice's phone (#00FF00) turns red and displays a '+' sign.
Alice's phone sends only the 'SK_t' (Secret Day Key) (#00BFFF) to a cloud icon labeled 'Public Server' (#FFFFFF).
The server shows a list containing 'SK_t', but highlights that no contact lists or names are uploaded.

sections.title: Step 4: Local Matching and Notification
lecture_lines: Users download daily keys of infected people.
Local devices re-generate potential IDs from these keys.
The phone checks for matches in local storage.
If a match is found, the user is notified.
Matching occurs entirely on the user's private device.
animations: Bob's phone (#FF00FF) downloads 'SK_t' from the Public Server.
Inside Bob's phone, a generator icon (#FF8C00) produces EphID_1, EphID_2, etc., from the downloaded 'SK_t'.
Bob's phone compares these generated IDs to its own 'Local Log'.
A match is found for 'EphID_A'. The log entry glows yellow (#FFFF00) to indicate the match.
A notification appears on Bob's phone: 'Potential Exposure Detected!' (#FF0000).

sections.title: Summary: Why It Works
lecture_lines: DP-3T balances public health with individual privacy.
Decentralization prevents mass surveillance by the state.
Security is maintained through local processing and cryptography.
animations: Show a simplified flow: Alice/Bob (ID Exchange) -> Alice (Sick) -> Server (Key) -> Bob (Match).
A green shield icon (#00FF00) appears over the entire process to represent security.
Final text: 'DP-3T: Protecting Health Without Sacrificing Liberty' (#FFFF00) in the center.
